scenes.text: You’ve probably seen modern concrete roads cracking after just a few years, but ancient Roman ruins are still standing strong after two thousand years.
For centuries, scientists were baffled, thinking the Romans were just lucky, but the secret is actually a genius mistake.
Inside Roman concrete are tiny, white mineral chunks called lime clasts, which researchers recently discovered are actually active self-healing agents.
When rainwater seeps into a crack, it dissolves the lime to seal it automatically, so hit follow to discover more ancient secrets!
